items.headline: US payrolls rise just 29,000 in September; unemployment ticks up to 4.2%
items.summary: September nonfarm payrolls grew 29,000, far below forecasts above 80,000, with the two prior months revised down and unemployment rising to 4.2%.
items.rationale: A cooling labour market eases pressure for more Fed tightening, pulling yields lower and supporting rate-sensitive sectors, while hinting at softer consumer demand ahead.

industries.why: Long-duration growth shares gain as yields fall
Softer loan demand, flatter rate outlook

economies.why: Hiring stalls as labour market cools

items.headline: Odds of an October Fed hike fall to about 17% from near 70% a week earlier
items.summary: After the jobs data, CME FedWatch put an October quarter-point hike at about 17%; prediction markets fell to 18% from almost 70%. A December hike is still priced. The Fed meets October 27–28.
items.rationale: A paused hiking cycle lowers short-term funding costs and supports equities, but December pricing keeps financing conditions tight into year-end.

industries.why: Growth valuations helped by lower rate path

economies.why: Less pressure from a stronger dollar

items.headline: US 10-year yield dips to about 5.18% after jobs data before rebounding with oil
items.summary: Treasury yields fell after the weak payrolls report, the 10-year touching about 5.18%, then rose again as oil climbed; the 30-year hovered near 5.63%.
items.rationale: Yields above 5% keep borrowing costs high across mortgages, corporate debt and emerging markets; volatility tied to oil makes the inflation-versus-growth trade-off harder to price.

economies.why: High US yields pressure capital flows

items.headline: Euro-area inflation jumps to 3.8% in September, highest since 2023, on energy costs
items.summary: Eurostat's flash estimate showed inflation at 3.8% from 3.2%, above the 3.6% forecast. Energy prices rose 18.8% on the year; core inflation edged up to 2.5%. The ECB hiked on 10 September.
items.rationale: Energy-led inflation strengthens the case for another ECB hike, raising borrowing costs while squeezing household real incomes and energy-intensive manufacturers.

industries.why: Energy costs and higher rates hit factories

economies.why: Stagflation risk as energy inflation spikes

items.headline: Iran attacks on Hormuz shipping reach about 40 a week; tankers hit, US weighs escorts
items.summary: Reports count roughly 40 drone and missile attacks a week on commercial ships; three tankers were attacked and one set ablaze. Washington says naval escorts with a coalition are possible and is sending a third carrier group.
items.rationale: Attacks raise freight and insurance costs and keep a risk premium in crude and LNG, hurting energy importers while lifting producers outside the Gulf.

industries.why: Higher energy inputs for smelters, chemicals

economies.why: Large crude importer exposed to Gulf

items.headline: Brent swings between about $100 and $103 a barrel as Gulf tensions persist
items.summary: Brent traded near $103 in the morning before settling around $99.68, down 2.6% on the day, after earlier jumping 5% on escalating attacks on Gulf shipping.
items.rationale: Crude near $100 feeds into fuel, freight and headline inflation, pressuring central banks and importers while supporting producer revenues.

industries.why: Jet and bunker fuel costs elevated

items.headline: US sanctions Iran's auto, rail and shadow banking networks as oil loadings hit zero
items.summary: The US Treasury's new action targets Iran's auto and rail sectors and a Russia-linked shadow banking network. Iran's tanker loadings fell to zero for the first time in the war under the US blockade at Kharg Island.
items.rationale: Removing Iranian barrels tightens supply further and raises enforcement risk for banks and traders handling sanctioned flows, notably in China.

items.headline: September LNG transits through Hormuz hit wartime high; crude exports near pre-war levels
items.summary: LNG shipments through the strait in September were the highest since the US-Iran war began, and crude exports have largely returned to pre-war levels. The US energy secretary says traffic is rising meaningfully.
items.rationale: Recovering volumes cap the supply shock and limit how far prices can spike, offsetting some of the attack-driven risk premium.

items.headline: China adds rate cuts and 700 billion yuan of extra relending in modest growth package
items.summary: The PBoC and regulators unveiled rate cuts, a 200 billion yuan rise in tech relending to 1.4 trillion and 500 billion more for farm and small-business relending, plus mortgage interest subsidies. Analysts call it modest.
items.rationale: Targeted credit supports infrastructure, computing and property demand at the margin, but its limited size caps the boost to commodity demand and global growth.

items.headline: Japan's large-manufacturer Tankan rises to 24 while yen weakens to about 158 per dollar
items.summary: The BoJ Tankan showed large manufacturers' sentiment at 24 from 22, but large non-manufacturers fell to 35 from 37. The yen hovered near 158.3, about four yen weaker than firms budgeted.
items.rationale: Firm sentiment and a weak yen keep another BoJ hike possible, while the softer yen lifts exporters' earnings and raises import costs for energy.

industries.why: Services sentiment weakens, import costs rise

items.headline: Economists expect RBI to raise repo rate to 5.5% on October 7 as rupee hovers near 96
items.summary: The RBI policy committee meets October 5–7. Economists expect a 25-basis-point hike from 5.25% after CPI inflation rose to 4.82% in August and the rupee slipped to about 96.1 per dollar.
items.rationale: Higher Indian rates aim to defend the rupee against oil-driven import costs, but raise borrowing costs for households and companies.

economies.why: Tightening amid oil and currency pressure

items.headline: UK 10-year gilt yield eases to 5.34% but is up 0.64 points over a year
items.summary: The 10-year gilt yield fell 5 basis points to 5.34% on October 2, but has risen 0.18 points in a month. The BoE plans £20 billion of annual active gilt sales.
items.rationale: Gilt yields above 5% keep UK mortgage and government borrowing costs high, weighing on housing and fiscal room.

industries.why: Mortgage rates tied to high gilt yields

items.headline: Chip stocks rally after a major memory maker says tight supply will last into 2028
items.summary: A leading memory chipmaker reported quarterly earnings per share up more than elevenfold and said memory supply would stay tight at least into 2028. A semiconductor index fund gained 11% in September and 3.6% in two October days.
items.rationale: Prolonged memory shortages lift chipmakers' pricing power and confirm durable AI investment, while raising component costs for device makers.

industries.why: AI demand keeps memory supply tight

economies.why: Chip and AI investment cycle stays strong
Higher memory costs for device assemblers

items.headline: Gold slips 0.9% to about $4,140 an ounce as dollar index holds near 2026 highs
items.summary: Gold fell 0.9% to $4,140 an ounce on October 2. The dollar index was about 102, after breaking above its May 2025 high this week, with Treasury yields elevated.
items.rationale: A firm dollar tightens conditions for importers and emerging-market borrowers, and pressures commodity prices priced in dollars.

economies.why: Strong dollar adds to rupee weakness

items.headline: More than 210 strikes hit Black Sea commercial ships in July–September, threatening grain
items.summary: A maritime risk firm counted over 210 strikes on commercial vessels in the Black Sea between July and September. Wheat is down 7% over the month but still about 32% higher than a year ago.
items.rationale: Disrupted Black Sea exports keep wheat and freight costs elevated, raising food import bills and food inflation risks.

industries.why: Higher grain input costs for processors
War-risk premiums in Black Sea shipping

economies.why: Large grain importers face higher bills
